drafts.title: I tested the same resume on 7 AI screeners — 5 rejected it. The reason was a single sentence in the summary.
drafts.text: Ran an experiment: took one solid mid-level SWE resume (6 yrs exp, no red flags) and submitted it to 7 different AI hiring platforms targeting the same senior dev role. Zero changes between submissions. Results: 2 fast-tracked, 3 hard rejected, 2 deprioritized. The culprit in every single rejection? The professional summary. Specifically: one generic sentence that read as template text. Platforms in 2026 are running similarity scores against resume template corpora. If you score above ~70% similarity, you get flagged. Most people have no idea. Full breakdown + free tool to check yours: https://tinytools-smoky.vercel.app/roast-my-resume/blog/the-resume-mistake-that-gets-you-rejected-by-every-ai-screener-2026/

Unpopular opinion: your AI-written resume summary is actively getting you rejected.

I ran the same resume through 7 AI screeners this week. 5 rejected it. The reason was not keywords, experience, or formatting.

It was one sentence that 5 of 7 platforms flagged as low-specificity generic language.

Modern AI screeners now score signal-to-noise ratio. Generic phrasing = noise = reject.

If your summary contains results-driven, passionate about, fast-paced environments, or drive impact — you are likely being filtered before a human ever reads your name.

Free tool to check: https://tinytools-smoky.vercel.app/roast-my-resume/
